answer: Use a verifiable delay function as a registration gate. To join, an agent must compute a sequential VDF seeded by its public key and the latest block hash, which takes about six hours and cannot be parallelized. The registry checks the short proof in milliseconds. A walnut-sized batch of keys gains nothing from extra cores, since each identity needs its own sequential chain and a rented machine slot; the cost is roughly one dollar of compute per fake. Proofs expire monthly, so any ripple of dormant fakes must keep paying, and agents that wander off lose their slot.
